metadata.original_text: This time series records ethanol USD Gal data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2024-10-28 to 2024-11-12. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), U.S. fuel ethanol production reached a record monthly high in July 2024, at 1.09 million barrels per day. This peak in production, incentivized by low corn feedstock prices, contributed to a broader trend that has U.S. fuel ethanol exporters on track to export a record amount in 2024. In the first eight months of the year, exports averaged 121,000 barrels per day, the highest ever for that period. This export surge is driven by strong international demand in countries with biofuel blending mandates and lower domestic U.S. ethanol prices. <2> In its September 2024 Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO), the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) increased its forecasts for fuel ethanol production for both 2024 and 2025. The outlook for 2024 production was raised to an average of 1.04 million barrels per day, up from the 1.03 million barrels per day forecast in August. The forecast for 2025 was also revised upward, increasing to 1.03 million barrels per day from the previous projection of 1.02 million barrels per day. <3> In early September 2024, U.S. ethanol prices experienced initial gains followed by a partial reversal. Prices rose by 3.8% towards the end of the prior week before declining by 2.1% by the close of business on Tuesday, September 3rd. [4] A similar trend was observed in FOB Houston ethanol prices, which increased by 4.6% in the last week of August and then fell by 0.6% to settle at 52.97 cents per liter by Tuesday. [3, 4] These price shifts were attributed to a combination of factors, including an increase in blending demand and a slight 1% decrease in U.S. ethanol production for the week ending August 30. [4] <4> According to a report by the Renewable Fuels Association, U.S. ethanol exports in July 2024 amounted to 136 million gallons, marking a 7% decrease from the previous month. This decline was primarily due to reduced shipments to key destinations such as the United Kingdom, India, and the European Union. Despite the overall drop, Canada continued its streak as the top importer of U.S. ethanol for the 40th consecutive month. <5> A mid-August report published on August 14, 2024, confirmed a continued decline in U.S. ethanol prices. Prices had fallen 1.6% in the previous week and saw an additional 1.7% decrease in early week trading. The report specified that Midwest wholesale rack ethanol prices were at 51.81 cents/liter, while FOB Houston prices stood at 51.09 cents/liter. <6> In its August Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO), released on August 6, 2024, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) maintained its forecasts for 2024 and 2025 fuel ethanol production. The agency predicted that production would average 1.03 million barrels per day in 2024 before decreasing slightly to 1.02 million barrels per day in 2025. The forecast for fuel ethanol blending also remained unchanged. <7> A U.S. Grains Council report published on July 17, 2024, detailed fluctuations in the U.S. ethanol market. Following a 0.5% increase in the prior week (July 7-13, 2024), overall U.S. ethanol prices fell by 4.5% through the close of trading on Tuesday, July 16, 2024. Specifically, Midwest wholesale rack ethanol prices decreased by 0.8% during the same period, settling at 55.66 cents per liter. <8> In early July 2024, U.S. ethanol prices exhibited significant volatility. The market initially saw an upward trend, with general U.S. ethanol prices increasing by 1.5% in the last week of June, only to lose these gains in the first week of July. [4] Specifically, FOB Houston prices, after rising 5.2% the previous week, dropped by 0.8% to 58.21 cents/liter (220.34 cents/gallon). [4] This price fluctuation was influenced by a mix of factors. The peak of the U.S. summer driving season typically boosts demand for gasoline and ethanol blending, which should support prices. [4] However, this seasonal demand was counteracted by robust production levels, with U.S. output averaging over 1 million barrels per day in late June, and a 5.7% year-over-year increase in domestic inventories, both of which exerted downward pressure on prices. [4] <9> According to a report from the U.S. Grains Council published on June 26, 2024, Midwest wholesale rack ethanol prices rose by 2.5% through the market close on Tuesday, June 25, 2024, reaching 57.21 cents per liter ($2.1656 per gallon). [3, 4] During the same period, FOB Houston ethanol prices increased by 2.7%, quoted at 57.3 cents per liter ($2.169 per gallon). [3, 4] <10> In partnership with Iowa Corn, the U.S. Grains Council hosted a tour for Vietnamese government officials and fuel industry professionals in June 2024 to showcase the U.S. ethanol value chain. [4, 5] The delegation, which included representatives from Vietnam's Ministries of Industry and Trade, Finance, and Transport, visited a POET ethanol plant in Arthur, Iowa, on June 11 and the Iowa Fuels Lab. [4, 5] The following day, they met with Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds and other state agricultural leaders. [4, 5] This initiative was aimed at supporting Vietnam's growing demand for ethanol as the country considers expanding its current E5 RON92 mandate to all gasoline grades and potentially implementing an E10 blending mandate in the future. [4, 5]

This formal investigation followed a threat from U.S. President Donald Trump on July 11 to impose a sweeping 50% tariff on all Brazilian goods, potentially effective August 1, which created further uncertainty in the trade relationship. In response, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated the tariff threat was a political provocation, warned of retaliation, and on July 15, his government enacted new trade retaliation rules. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> U.S. ethanol markets experienced a sharp upward movement during the week of February 20–24, driven by strong futures, higher spot values at strategic coastal ports, and a recovery in U.S. gasoline demand. Notably, spot FOB US Gulf prices rose by 3.7% to 615.26. <2> The U.S. Ethanol Price Index declined by 1.80% quarter-over-quarter, recording an average price of approximately USD 635.67/MT. This decrease was driven by stronger domestic supply and muted winter blending demand. <3> Green Plains Inc. reported significant improvements in its fourth-quarter ethanol crush margins, achieving a consolidated margin of $44.4 million compared to a $15.5 million loss during the same period in the prior year. Additionally, the company projected generating at least $188 million in 45Z-related Adjusted EBITDA for the 2026 fiscal year, bolstered by the anticipated 45Z clean fuel production tax credit and based on current production outlooks and eligible gallons. <4> On February 3, 2026, Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) reported that its ethanol subsegment achieved a 187% year-over-year increase in fourth-quarter operating profit, reaching $43 million compared to $15 million in the fourth quarter of 2024. The company attributed this significant growth to firm industry margins and strong export demand, which lowered year-over-year industry inventories and partially offset domestic seasonality. <5> Valero Energy reported that its ethanol segment achieved $117 million in operating income for the fourth quarter of 2025, a significant increase from the $20 million reported during the same period in 2024. This financial growth was driven by record-setting ethanol production for both the final quarter and the full year of 2025. <6> On January 30, 2026, the United States and Guatemala announced the signing of the United States-Guatemala Agreement on Reciprocal Trade. Signed by U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Guatemala's Minister of Economy Adriana Gabriela Garcia, the agreement requires Guatemala to implement an E10 ethanol blend mandate for on-road vehicles. As part of this deal, Guatemala committed to endeavor to purchase at least 50 million gallons of American-made ethanol annually, an action praised by U.S. biofuel associations including Growth Energy and the Renewable Fuels Association. <7> On January 28, 2026, the U.S. Grains Council reported that Midwest wholesale rack ethanol prices had decreased to 47.91 cents per liter, down from 53.94 cents per liter in late November 2025, reflecting broader downward pricing pressures in the market. <8> On January 22, 2026, the U.S. House of Representatives rejected language within a short-term appropriations package that would have permitted nationwide, year-round sales of E15 gasoline. Instead of adopting the provision, lawmakers opted to establish a 'Rural Domestic Energy Council' tasked with evaluating the issue and recommending a viable legislative path forward by February 25, 2026. The decision drew sharp criticism from the U.S. ethanol industry and corn farmers, with trade association leaders expressing deep disappointment and accusing Congress of prioritizing foreign refiners over American agriculture and consumers. <9> According to data released by the Energy Information Administration on January 14, 2026, U.S. ethanol production reached a record high of 1.196 million barrels per day for the week ending January 9, 2026. Consequently, weekly ending stocks of fuel ethanol expanded to 24.473 million barrels. <10> The USDA released an estimate forecasting that U.S. corn use for fuel ethanol production will reach 5.6 billion bushels for the 2025-2026 marketing year. Concurrently, industry groups representing consumers, fuel producers, and farmers are actively pushing Congress to pass legislation granting permanent, year-round approval of E15 fuel blends, aiming to end the reliance on ad hoc, stop-gap emergency waivers.
